To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
host population density and host body mass are important predictors of parasite species richness in primates, but that these variables are confounded with phylogeny.

(1) parasite diversity in anthropoid primates is correlated with host population density, (2) the relationship between parasite diversity and host body mass is an artifact of phylogeny, (3) the correlation between parasite diversity and diet is not robust to phylogeny, and (4) habitat diversity is not associated with parasite diversity.

host population density is associated consistently with the total number of parasites in a species' parasite community and the diversity of several parasite taxa, whereas host body mass is correlated only weakly and inconsistently with parasite species richness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diversity of parasite species in primates and with the factors that determine the number of parasite taxa that infect a given host species.
the factors that determine the number and types of parasites in a species.
the factors determining parasite diversity in primates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
host population density is a strong predictor of parasite species richness in primates, and that this association is independent of host body mass and phylogenetic relatedness.
population density is the strongest predictor of parasite community diversity among anthropoid primates.
host population density is the best predictor of total parasite diversity and that host body mass is the best predictor among the life‐history variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diversity of parasites in primates is determined by a combination of host body mass, host population density, and the diversity of viruses.
host body mass, population density, and geographic range size are the most important predictors of total parasite diversity in primates.
the diversity of parasite communities in primates is best explained by a combination of host population density and body mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
host body mass is not the most important determinant of total parasite diversity or the diversity of individual parasite taxa in anthropoid primates.
parasite species richness is a product of the host's population density and the parasite's transmission mode.
the diversity of parasites in anthropoid primates is strongly associated with host population density and the diversity of viral parasites.
